references.text: The Levites obeyed Moses' command to punish the idolaters after the golden calf incident, even when it involved their own family members, thus showing loyalty to God's covenant over family ties.
Aaron and his sons were commanded not to mourn Nadab and Abihu in the usual way, but to prioritize their service to the Lord over family grief.
Phinehas showed zeal for the Lord by acting against sinners, even at the cost of social bonds, and received the promise of an eternal priestly covenant.
The covenant with Levi meant that the Levites were to preserve knowledge and be messengers of the Lord's word, which required complete devotion.
Jesus taught that whoever loves father or mother more than him is not worthy of him—a principle reflecting the Levites' prioritization of God over family.
Jesus defined his true family as those who do God's will, showing that spiritual loyalty surpasses biological bonds.
Jesus said that anyone who does not hate their father, mother, wife, children, and siblings cannot be his disciple—a radical call to put God first.
